target_claim: The explicit four-move crossing schedule is safe for any vertex cover S with |S| <= k-1, and hence (G,K) has a vertex cover of size <= K iff the river-crossing instance (G, k=K+1) is feasible.
source_quote:
At every departure, the bank left behind is independent (either I with one
fewer element, or a singleton {x}), so the safety constraint holds throughout by Lemma 1.
test_sketch: Implement (i) the literal four-move schedule from lines 0061-0080 with a bank-state simulator that checks independence of the Charon-free bank at every departure, and (ii) a brute-force BFS feasibility oracle over all states (left-set, right-set, Charon side) for n <= 12. Input family: star graphs K_{1,m} (center c adjacent to leaves), S = {c}, K = 1, k = 2. For K_{1,3} (n = 4): in cycle 2, Step 2 departs the right bank leaving {c, x1} where c and x1 are adjacent -- the simulator flags a safety violation, refuting the quoted claim. The BFS oracle further shows (K_{1,3}, k=2) is infeasible even though tau(K_{1,3}) = 1 <= K, refuting equivalence (1) itself (the known Alcuin-number tau+2 phenomenon).
